description: Conchas are iconic Mexican sweet bread, known for their soft, fluffy texture and a distinctive shell-like sugary topping. This traditional pan dulce offers a delightful balance of sweetness, perfect for dipping in coffee or hot chocolate. Experience a taste of Mexico's rich baking heritage with these beautiful and flavorful conchas.

instructions.title: Activate the Yeast
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine the warm milk, 1 tablespoon of granulated sugar, and the active dry yeast. Stir gently and let it sit for 5-10 minutes until foamy. This indicates the yeast is active.

instructions.title: Prepare the Dough
instructions.text: Add the remaining granulated sugar, eggs, softened butter, salt, and vanilla extract to the yeast mixture. Gradually add the 4 cups of all-purpose flour, mixing until a shaggy dough forms. Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured surface and knead for 8-10 minutes until it is smooth and elastic. Place the dough in a greased bowl, cover with plastic wrap, and let it rise in a warm place for 1-2 hours, or until doubled in size.

instructions.title: Make the Concha Topping
instructions.text: While the dough is rising, prepare the topping. In a medium bowl, combine the powdered sugar, softened vegetable shortening, and 1 cup of all-purpose flour. Mix with your hands until a smooth, paste-like dough forms. Divide the topping dough into two equal portions if making two colors. For chocolate conchas, knead 1 tablespoon of cocoa powder into one portion. Roll each portion into a log and divide into 12 equal pieces.

instructions.title: Shape the Conchas
instructions.text: Once the dough has doubled, gently punch it down and divide it into 12 equal pieces. Roll each piece into a smooth ball. Place the dough balls on baking sheets lined with parchment paper, leaving space between them. Flatten each ball slightly.

instructions.title: Apply the Topping and Score
instructions.text: Take one piece of the topping dough and flatten it into a thin disc, slightly larger than the dough ball. Carefully place the topping disc over a dough ball, pressing gently to adhere. Use a concha cutter or a small knife to score a shell pattern onto the topping. Be careful not to cut through the bread dough itself, only the topping. Repeat for all conchas. Cover the baking sheets with plastic wrap and let the conchas rise for another 45-60 minutes, or until visibly puffy.

instructions.title: Bake the Conchas
instructions.text: Preheat your oven to 350F (175C). Bake the conchas for 18-22 minutes, or until the bread is golden brown on the bottom and the topping is set. The topping should not brown significantly. Remove from the oven and transfer to a wire rack to cool completely before serving. Enjoy your delicious homemade Conchas!

tips: Ensure your milk is at the correct temperature for activating yeast; too hot will kill it, too cold won't activate it.
For perfectly round topping discs, place a piece of topping dough between two sheets of parchment paper and roll it out with a rolling pin.
Store cooled conchas in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 3 days. They also freeze well for longer storage.
